newsitem.title: UK: Zinc price should improve in 1997 - Billiton.
newsitem.headline: Zinc price should improve in 1997 - Billiton.

text.p: Improving demand will help to accelerate the drawdown in zinc inventories as this year draws to a close, helping prices in 1997 and 1998, London Metal Exchange (LME) trader Billiton Metals Ltd said.

Demand this year has been mixed -- the U.S. has been strong, but Japan has disappointed. European demand has yet to live up to expectations and some de-stocking has been seen in other Far Eastern countries.
"Nevertheless the market has remained in deficit this year thanks to a large extent to the fact that refined production levels in the West have fallen short of envisaged levels."
Billiton said mine production levels have been lower than anticipated, although new capacity should ensure that output continues to rise next year.
Refined stocks currently stand at just below nine weeks consumption, against an end-1995 level of just under 10 weeks, indicating that the stock drawdown process has been slow.
But better demand will accelerate the stock downtrend towards the end of the year and this will remain the case going into 1997, so prices will gradually improve next year.

"Furthermore, the market should end 1997 on a high note, as by that stage inventory levels are likely to have been reduced to much more comfortable levels, thus paving the way for further improvement in 1998," Billiton said.
